title: Counting Guidance for High Fidelity Text-to-Image Synthesis
reads: Pretrained class-agnostic RCC reads the decoded clean-image estimate at every step, masked by each word's attention map when the prompt has two object types; it never reads noisy features
trained_on: nothing trained; RCC is used pretrained with a hand-written squared relative count loss
gradient_enters: epsilon <- epsilon + s_count sqrt(1 - alpha_bar_t) grad_{z_t} L_count on all 50 DDIM steps, s_count = 1 or max(0.01, 0.2N - 1), no cap
unseen: no; 34 prompt classes with no split into classes RCC saw and did not see
headline: Normalised MAE (count error divided by target, lower is better) 0.567 against 0.599 for vanilla Stable Diffusion on 680 prompts; at count 2 the plotted error rises from about 0.47 unguided to about 0.54 at s_count 1.0
copy_or_avoid: Avoid a decoded-image counter at early steps and a strong push at count 2, where this paper's error rises with guidance strength (inferred)

extra_papers.title: Learning to Count Anything: Reference-less Class-agnostic Counting with Weak Supervision (RCC)

extra_papers.title: Teaching CLIP to Count to Ten
extra_papers.why: Trains a counting-aware CLIP model, an abstract property across categories (described on p. 3)

disagreements.claim: Counting Guidance optimises the latent using a density map
disagreements.paper_says: The counter is RCC, which retrieves the count directly by regression, in contrast to most heatmap-based counters

disagreements.claim: Counting Guidance requires an additional U-Net in every denoising step
disagreements.paper_says: Algorithm 1 calls the denoising network once per step, then the decoder and RCC; no second U-Net appears

disagreements.claim: Object masks come from self-attention maps
disagreements.paper_says: Section 4.2.2 builds one map per object word and excludes the sot token as Attend-and-Excite does, which describes cross-attention (inferred)
